Attachment-4: Permitting Study & Review 2 DE-FE0031937 / 0005 1.0 Background Dastur International Inc. has designed and engineered a solution that maximizes the decarbonization of available BF gas by capturing 2.8 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of carbon dioxide (CO ) emissions from 2 blast furnaces (BFs) at Cleveland-Cliffs’ 5-million tonnes/year steel production plant in Burns Harbor, Indiana. This includes the design and integration of an optimum BF gas flow distribution system, an innovative BF gas conditioning process, an efficient solvent-based carbon capture technology, and an economical steam and power generation system. The proposed carbon capture scheme envisaged at Burns Harbor is depicted in Figure 1. The available BF gas (Stream 1) is tapped from the BF header and undergoes a compositional shift by passing it through a series of Water Gas Shift (WGS) Reactors, which converts ~80% of the carbon monoxide (CO) in the BF gas to CO (Stream 2). The increase in CO content (22% in BF gas vs. 32% after the WGS unit) in the shifted 2 2 gas enables the capture of up to 85% of CO e in the available BF gas, with benefits of lower capture island 2 footprint, single train, lower CAPEX and easier fit within the space-constrained Burns Harbor plant. The post-capture H -rich fuel gas (H RF or Stream 3) is sent to the existing powerhouse to produce captive 2 2 power for in-plant use; the use of the H -rich fuel gas instead of the BF gas (present scenario) in the 2 powerhouse does not require any modification to the existing burners, thus minimizing disruptions to existing operations.
